$comment: Why each family in the current season is there. validate:rationale checks pool membership, cited scenarios, sub-skills and audience counts. Whether a family is fun, and whether a ladder that mixes authors is in the right order, hasn't been playtested yet.
$evidence: Three kinds, strongest first. A benchmark author's published design note says what the scenario was built to test, from the person who built it. KovaaK's in-game scenario description comes next and is first-party for scenarios no benchmark documents. Community discussion comes last and is only used where it says something the other two don't, which is mostly about scenarios older than the benchmarks that later picked them up. Where a family's evidence is thin, it gets a 'thin' note.
$audience: Audience figures reproduce the committed KovaaK's taxonomy snapshot; they are not live counts or evidence that a scenario is enjoyable.

families.isolates: Two static targets close together. The hard part is the short flick between them.
families.why: The classic two-target flick, and the static test with the most agreement behind it: Lemon, snakbox, Aimerz+ and Viscose all grade a 1w2ts Perfected cut. The flick is shorter than in the wide-wall families, so stopping matters more than travel. The Novice rung is a jumbo Tile Frenzy cut nobody grades, because none of those four sheets goes below its own entry tier.

families.isolates: Static clicking along a diagonal path, so you're moving on both axes at once.
families.why: The diagonal ClickTrack path, which works both mouse axes at once. That's why there's an axis family besides Horizontal. Its Expert board is the thinnest in the season and is kept on a written exception: the lineage has three cuts above the Expert floor and Triangle and Horizontal already use two of them. If the boards grow, the exception goes away.

evidence.says: Grades "ClickTrack Diagonal 2t" in its Static tier, filed under Normal.

families.isolates: Static clicking along one horizontal line: no vertical correction, just travel and stopping.
families.why: ClickTrack along one axis: no vertical correction, just travel and stopping. Apart from Triangle it's the only ClickTrack axis family whose boards reach the Expert floor, which is why it stayed and Vertical didn't. Same caveat as Triangle: TSK Mixed grades the lineage but bands it by category name, so the difficulty order is the lineage's own, shorter to longer travel and three targets to two.

evidence.says: Grades "ClickTrack Horizontal 2t" in its Static tier, filed under Normal.

families.isolates: Static clicking on targets smaller than a comfortable stop, so overshoot is most of the difficulty.
families.why: Only the hard end of micro clicking is graded (Aimerz+ S1 and Anima Micro, both near the top of this ladder), so the family is built down from a graded Expert rung instead of up from a graded Novice one. The other static families go the other way, and this is why two of its four rungs are hand-picked. Nothing else in the pool covers it: at these sizes tremor in the stop limits you far more than travel speed.

families.isolates: Micro clicking on a shot clock, so a miss also costs you the time to recover.
families.why: Micro clicking with a shot clock. cA Static S1 and Aimerz+ Static Clicking both grade the fuglaapressure lineage. With the clock you have to recover from a miss inside the same window, which the untimed Micro family doesn't test. The easy rung is the lineage author's own supereasy cut, made for people who can't hold the graded ones yet, so it works as a Novice rung.

families.isolates: Raw click rate on targets that are already easy to hit. No benchmark grades it.
families.why: The only family in the pool no benchmark sheet grades at any difficulty. It's in anyway because people test raw click speed on easy targets all the time and the sheets don't cover it, so all four rungs are picked by hand and the family is marked thin. 1wall9000targets is the reference scenario and has a bigger board than most graded scenarios in this season.

evidence.says: 108,729 players have posted a score on it, more than most graded scenarios in this season. No benchmark tier, but plenty of people play it.

families.thin: No benchmark sheet grades this lineage at any difficulty, so there's no design note to cite and the family rests on the pool's own reading of the test. That's a gap in the sheets. It says nothing about the scenario.

families.isolates: Static clicking around three fixed points, so the way back counts as much as the way out.
families.why: The unsuffixed ClickTrack cuts, which have the deepest boards in the lineage and are the only ones that reach the Expert board floor. Three fixed points instead of a line, so the return path counts too; that's the difference from Horizontal. TSK Mixed is the only sheet with ClickTrack at all, and it names its tiers after categories, so the rungs follow the lineage's own order with no published tier behind it.

evidence.says: Grades "ClickTrack 3t" in its Static tier, filed under Normal.

families.isolates: Wide static clicking on a shot clock, with flicks long enough to plan.
families.why: Wide static clicking with a shot clock, and the family with the most varied sources: Revosect S5 grades the entry and intermediate cuts, cA Static S1 and Aimerz+ Static Clicking grade the hard ones. The difference from Micro Pressure is spacing. The flicks are long enough to plan, so the clock is on your plan more than your tremor.

families.isolates: Static clicking over long travel, on scenarios that don't reward dropping your sensitivity.
families.why: A static family should measure clicking and not pathing, and shouldn't reward a sensitivity nobody plays at. The Novice rung comes from Avasive, a sheet this pool doesn't list as a source, so it's admitted on the shape of the test and not on Avasive's grading.
